subject: English
stem: I asked two people the way to the station ___
optA: but neither of them could help me
optB: however none of them could show me the way
optC: yet they had doubts about the station
solution: For exactly two people the correct pronoun is 'neither' (not 'none', used for more than two), and 'but neither of them could help me' reads coherently. Matches option A.

subject: English
stem: The room was very warm ___
optA: because the AC was set to moderate temperature
optB: though the AC was set to very cold
optC: since the AC was not very warm in its temperature setting
optD: since the AC was in a very low temperature setting
solution: The room being warm needs a logical cause; a moderate (not cold) AC setting explains the warmth, while options C and D imply cooling and contradict the sentence. Matches option A.

subject: English
stem: We could leave today or we could leave tomorrow ___
optB: as you prefer one of the two
solution: After presenting two options, the idiomatic completion is 'whichever you prefer'. Matches option D.

subject: English
stem: Mohan and I couldn't get into the house because ___
optA: neither of us had the keys
optB: both of us do not have the keys
optC: either of us did not have the keys
optD: neither of us did have the keys
solution: 'Neither of us had the keys' uses correct negative + past tense; the other options are ungrammatical or illogical. Matches option A.

subject: English
stem: There are many good hotels, you can choose to stay in ___
solution: Choosing a single hotel out of many is expressed as 'any one of them'; 'either' is only for two, and 'many/all of them' contradict choosing one. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: The general tone of the passage is that of
solution: The passage speaks of a 'positive outlook', recovering confidence and 'pent-up demand', all conveying optimism. Matches option A.

subject: English
stem: The willingness of consumers to go back to normal lifestyle indicates their
solution: The passage links renewed spending to 'increased confidence about the future of the economy', i.e. a sense of economic security. Matches option D.

subject: English
stem: Which statement in the passage indicates that 'Life must go on'?
optA: They settled into their new routines
optB: Salary cuts could be coming to an end
optC: People are moving on with their lives
solution: The phrase 'moving on with their lives' directly conveys that 'Life must go on'. Matches option C.

subject: English
stem: What does the author mean by 'pent-up demand'?
optA: Desire (suppressed) to spend money once pandemic is controlled
optD: Criticism of the public on the pay-cuts
solution: The passage defines pent-up demand as suppressed demand that 'could be unleashed once a vaccine is developed', i.e. a held-back desire to spend once the pandemic is controlled. Matches option A.

subject: English
stem: What, according to the author, is the reason behind suppression of consumer demands?
optA: The lack of vaccine till date
optC: Motive to save up some money
optD: Careful and calculative attitude of the general public
solution: The passage attributes suppressed demand to 'fears of job losses and salary cuts', i.e. professional insecurity. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: Everything is going well; (a) we didn't have (b) any problem. (c) No error. (d)
solution: The present situation ('is going well') requires the present tense 'we don't have', not the past 'didn't have'. Error lies in segment (b). Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: Lavanya hasn't gone (a) to work (b) yesterday. (c) No error. (d)
solution: The past-time marker 'yesterday' requires simple past ('didn't go'), not the present perfect 'hasn't gone'. Error lies in segment (a). Matches option A.

subject: English
stem: Look! The boy over there (a) wears the same sweater (b) as you. (c) No error. (d)
solution: 'Look!' signals an action happening now, requiring present continuous 'is wearing', not simple present 'wears'. Error lies in segment (b). Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: It begins (a) to turn dark: (b) shall I switch on the lights? (c) No error. (d)
optC: shall I switch on the lights?
solution: A change happening at the moment of speaking requires present continuous 'It is beginning', not simple present 'It begins'. Error lies in segment (a). Matches option A.

subject: English
stem: Raman and Mitali (a) have been married (b) for twenty years. (c) No error. (d)
solution: Present perfect 'have been married for twenty years' correctly expresses a state continuing up to now; the sentence is correct. Matches option D.

subject: English
stem: I have played (a) basketball (b) for the past three hours. (c) No error. (d)
solution: An activity continuing over 'the past three hours' needs present perfect continuous 'I have been playing', not present perfect 'I have played'. Error lies in segment (a). Matches option A.

subject: English
stem: Jamila had a book (a) in front of her, (b) but she didn't read it. (c) No error. (d)
solution: All verbs are consistently in the simple past and the sentence is grammatically sound. Matches option D.

subject: English
stem: When she heard the news (a) she hasn't been (b) very pleased. (c) No error. (d)
solution: The past clause 'When she heard' requires simple past 'she wasn't', not present perfect 'she hasn't been'. Error lies in segment (b). Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: Where are you coming from? (a) Are you (b) an American? (c) No error. (d)
solution: Asking about origin/nationality needs simple present 'Where do you come from?', not present continuous 'Where are you coming from?'. Error lies in segment (a). Matches option A.

subject: English
stem: I went to Canada (a) a few years ago (b) for a holiday. (c) No error. (d)
solution: Simple past 'went' correctly agrees with the past-time marker 'a few years ago'; the sentence is correct. Matches option D.

subject: English
stem: from Europe to America (P)/ in 1992 (Q)/ his first voyage (R)/ Columbus made (S)
solution: Correct order: 'Columbus made (S) his first voyage (R) from Europe to America (P) in 1992 (Q)' = SRPQ. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: scientists have (P)/ the effects of (Q)/ warned us about (R)/ climate change (S)
solution: Correct order: 'scientists have (P) warned us about (R) the effects of (Q) climate change (S)' = PRQS. Matches option C.

subject: English
stem: speed is a potent cause (P)/ industrial growth at a terrific (Q)/ in a big city (R)/ of pollution (S)
solution: Correct order: 'industrial growth at a terrific (Q) speed is a potent cause (P) of pollution (S) in a big city (R)' = QPSR. Matches option D.

subject: English
stem: and garbage (P)/ today our environment (Q)/ filth and squalor (R)/ is in constant grip of (S)
solution: Correct order: 'today our environment (Q) is in constant grip of (S) filth and squalor (R) and garbage (P)' = QSRP. Matches option D.

subject: English
stem: of corruption everywhere (P)/ to ease out (Q)/ the monster (R)/ it is the duty of the government (S)
solution: Correct order: 'it is the duty of the government (S) to ease out (Q) the monster (R) of corruption everywhere (P)' = SQRP. Matches option A.

subject: English
stem: Forty winks
optD: A short sleep during the day
solution: 'Forty winks' means a short nap, especially during the day. Matches option D.

subject: English
stem: Life in the raw
optA: Life in its natural, unembellished state
solution: 'Life in the raw' means life in its natural, harsh, unembellished state. Matches option A.

subject: English
stem: A paper tiger
optA: A person or thing that appears threatening but is ineffectual
optB: To threaten someone but do nothing
optD: To speak to people in a roaring voice
solution: 'A paper tiger' is something that seems threatening but is actually powerless or ineffectual. Matches option A.

subject: English
stem: Penny-wise and pound-foolish
optA: Wise to spend each penny carefully
optB: Careful about small amounts but careless about large amounts
optC: People who don't understand the importance of each penny
optD: Careful about large amounts but careless about small amounts
solution: 'Penny-wise and pound-foolish' describes being careful about small sums while wasteful with large ones. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: Pin back your ears
optB: Person or organisation that pins important issues
optC: To keep yourself away from hearing bad stuff
optD: To clean your ears with a pin
solution: 'Pin back your ears' means to listen very carefully. Matches option A.

subject: English
stem: Turncoat
optB: Someone who deserts one group to join another
optD: Going round and round in a court of law
solution: A 'turncoat' is a person who abandons one party or cause to join the opposing one. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: about (R)/ climate change (S)
solution: The source prints only fragments R and S; treating it as the intended repeat of the 'scientists have / the effects of / warned us about / climate change' item, the correct order is PRQS. Matches option C.
reviewNote: SOURCE-TRUNCATED: the source doc prints this item (setcounter 31 -> Q32) with only 'about (R)/ climate change (S)' visible and the same options as Q22. It is a truncated duplicate of Q22 and is unanswerable as printed; keyed C to match Q22's intended answer (PRQS). Needs human review.

subject: English
stem: speed is a potent cause (P)/ industrial growth at a terrific (Q)/ in a big city (R)/ of pollution (S)
solution: Correct order: 'industrial growth at a terrific (Q) speed is a potent cause (P) of pollution (S) in a big city (R)' = QPSR. Matches option D.
reviewNote: Internal duplicate of Q23 (the source doc repeats the jumbled-words block); stem and options are identical to Q23.

subject: English
stem: and garbage (P)/ today our environment (Q)/ filth and squalor (R)/ is in constant grip of (S)
solution: Correct order: 'today our environment (Q) is in constant grip of (S) filth and squalor (R) and garbage (P)' = QSRP. Matches option D.
reviewNote: Internal duplicate of Q24 (the source doc repeats the jumbled-words block); stem and options are identical to Q24.

subject: English
stem: of corruption everywhere (P)/ to ease out (Q)/ the monster (R)/ it is the duty of the government (S)
solution: Correct order: 'it is the duty of the government (S) to ease out (Q) the monster (R) of corruption everywhere (P)' = SQRP. Matches option A.
reviewNote: Internal duplicate of Q25 (the source doc repeats the jumbled-words block); stem and options are identical to Q25.

subject: English
stem: Honesty is ___ on his face.
solution: The passive construction 'Honesty is written on his face' requires the past participle 'written'. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: He lives ___ his pen.
solution: The set phrase 'to live by one's pen' means to earn a living through writing. Matches option A.

subject: English
stem: Much water has run ___ bridge since then.
solution: The idiom is 'much water has run under the bridge', meaning much time has passed. Matches option C.

subject: English
stem: The gun ___ with a loud noise.
solution: The phrasal verb 'went off' means fired/exploded, fitting 'with a loud noise'. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: They fought ___ the last man in the army.
solution: The idiom is 'fought to the last man', meaning until everyone was gone. Matches option D.

subject: English
stem: He DROWNED in the flood water last year. Choose the word most similar in meaning to DROWNED.
solution: 'Drowned' (sank and died under water) is closest to 'submerged'. Matches option C.

subject: English
stem: Autumn is rather a DRY season. Choose the word most similar in meaning to DRY.
solution: 'Dry' is synonymous with 'arid'; humid, rainy and moist are opposites. Matches option A.

subject: English
stem: Our DIFFERENCES are growing day by day. Choose the word most similar in meaning to DIFFERENCES.
solution: In the sense of interpersonal conflict, 'differences' means 'disagreements'; 'discrepancies' denotes inconsistencies, not disputes. Matches option C.

subject: English
stem: The big tree HINDERED access of sunlight into the house. Choose the word most similar in meaning to HINDERED.
solution: 'Hindered' (obstructed) is synonymous with 'impeded'; 'facilitated' is its opposite. Matches option A.

subject: English
stem: The COMPLEXITY of the issue baffled everyone. Choose the word most similar in meaning to COMPLEXITY.
solution: 'Complexity' means 'intricacy'; complacency is a similar-sounding distractor with an unrelated meaning. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: I am very PARTICULAR about it. Choose the word most opposite in meaning to PARTICULAR.
solution: 'Particular' (specific, exact) is opposite to 'vague'; 'precise' is a synonym. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: He has become PAUNCHY. Choose the word most opposite in meaning to PAUNCHY.
solution: 'Paunchy' (having a fat belly) is opposite to 'slim'; stout, plump and fat are synonyms. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: This river ORIGINATES from the Ganges. Choose the word most opposite in meaning to ORIGINATES.
solution: 'Originates' (begins) is opposite to 'culminates' (ends); inaugurates, initiates and emanates are near-synonyms of beginning/flowing from. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem: The film I saw was HILARIOUS. Choose the word most opposite in meaning to HILARIOUS.
solution: 'Hilarious' (extremely funny) is opposite to 'serious'; uproarious and jovial are synonyms. Matches option B.
reviewNote: Ambiguous key: both 'serious' (printed option B) and 'tragic' (printed option A) are defensible antonyms of hilarious. Chose the dictionary-standard antonym 'serious' (B); 'tragic' (A) is a close second via the comedy-vs-tragedy film contrast. Needs human confirmation.

subject: English
stem: On that day, PANDEMONIUM reigned in the hall. Choose the word most opposite in meaning to PANDEMONIUM.
solution: 'Pandemonium' (chaos and uproar) is opposite to 'peace'; hullaballoo and uproar are synonyms. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Indian Rivers, Lakes and Water Bodies
stem: Which one of the following is NOT a tributary of the Indus River?
solution: Tawi is a tributary of the Chenab, not directly of the Indus; Beas, Ravi and Chenab are direct tributaries of the Indus. Matches option D.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Indian Rivers, Lakes and Water Bodies
stem: River Beas, flowing from Himachal Pradesh and Punjab, joins the river:
solution: The Beas joins the Satluj (Sutlej) near Harike in Punjab. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Indian Rivers, Lakes and Water Bodies
stem: Which one of the following rivers was earlier known as "Vitasta"?
solution: The Jhelum in Kashmir was known as Vitasta in ancient Sanskrit texts. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Indian Rivers, Lakes and Water Bodies
stem:
Consider the following facts of the rivers of the Indus system:
1. The Satluj originates in Tibet where it is known as Langchen Khambab.
2. The Satluj is a classic example of an antecedent river.
3. The Jhelum is the largest tributary of the Indus system.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution: The Satluj is called Langchen Khambab in Tibet (1 correct) and is a classic antecedent river (2 correct); the Chenab, not the Jhelum, is the largest tributary of the Indus (3 wrong). Matches option C.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Indian Rivers, Lakes and Water Bodies
stem: Brahmaputra and Indus rivers are antecedent rivers. Which one of the following may be the true definition of antecedent drainage?
optA: Which follows the initial slope of the Himalaya
optB: Which existed before the Himalayan range came into existence
optC: Which followed the dip of rock beds of the Himalaya
optD: Which followed the strike of rock beds of the Himalaya
solution: Antecedent drainage means a river that existed before the mountain range was uplifted and kept its course through the rising land. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Indian Rivers, Lakes and Water Bodies
stem: Which one of the following Himalayan rivers does NOT originate from across the Himalayas?
solution: Indus, Satluj and Brahmaputra rise on the Tibetan plateau across the Himalayas; the Ganga rises from the Gangotri glacier within the Himalayas. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Indian Rivers, Lakes and Water Bodies
stem:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (River Basin)
A. Bhagirathi
B. Alaknanda
C. Nayar
D. Ganga
List-II (Town)
1. Lansdowne
2. Narendra Nagar
3. Uttarkashi
4. Pauri
solution: Uttarkashi lies on the Bhagirathi (A-3), Pauri is in the Alaknanda basin (B-4), Lansdowne is near the Nayar (C-1) and Narendra Nagar overlooks the Ganga (D-2). Matches option B.
reviewNote: Bank row 7695c15c keys the identical option order as C (A-2,B-4,C-1,D-3), which places Narendra Nagar with the Bhagirathi and Uttarkashi with the Ganga. Uttarkashi is firmly on the Bhagirathi (forces A-3), so bank key C is structurally impossible; derived correct answer is B. Possible bank wrong-key.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Indian Rivers, Lakes and Water Bodies
stem:
Which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. Chambal and Betwa are tributaries of Yamuna.
2. Yamuna is the largest tributary of Ganga.
3. Chambal and Betwa join the Ganga directly in Uttar Pradesh.
solution: Chambal and Betwa are tributaries of the Yamuna (1 correct); the Yamuna is the largest tributary of the Ganga (2 correct); Chambal and Betwa join the Yamuna, not the Ganga directly (3 wrong). Matches option B.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Indian Rivers, Lakes and Water Bodies
stem: Which one of the following rivers is NOT a tributary of Brahmaputra?
solution: Manas, Kameng and Subansiri are tributaries of the Brahmaputra; the Mahananda is a tributary of the Ganga. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Indian Rivers, Lakes and Water Bodies
stem:
Which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. Tsangpo crosses over into India under the name of Dihang.
2. River Chambal and River Betwa are important tributaries of River Yamuna.
3. River Subansiri is a tributary of River Ganga.
solution: The Tsangpo enters India as the Dihang (1 correct); Chambal and Betwa are tributaries of the Yamuna (2 correct); the Subansiri is a tributary of the Brahmaputra, not the Ganga (3 wrong). Matches option B.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Indian Rivers, Lakes and Water Bodies
stem:
Consider the following statements regarding Brahmaputra:
1. It rises in Tibet, near Lake Mansarovar.
2. It takes a "U" turn near Namcha Barwa and enters India through a gorge.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution: The Brahmaputra rises in Tibet near Lake Mansarovar (1) and takes a U-turn near Namcha Barwa to enter India through a gorge (2); both correct. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Indian Rivers, Lakes and Water Bodies
stem: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
solution: Godavari-Wainganga, Cauvery-Bhavani and Krishna-Bhima are correct; Amaravati is a tributary of the Cauvery, not the Narmada, so Narmada-Amaravati is wrong. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Indian Rivers, Lakes and Water Bodies
stem: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
solution: Penganga belongs to the Godavari system, not the Ganga, so Ganga-Penganga is incorrectly matched. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Indian Rivers, Lakes and Water Bodies
stem: Which one of the following is NOT a tributary of Cauvery?
solution: Indravati is a tributary of the Godavari, not the Cauvery; Hemavati, Arkavati and Amaravati are Cauvery tributaries. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Indian Rivers, Lakes and Water Bodies
stem:
How many of the following statements are correct?
1. Sharavati river creates Jog Falls.
2. Brahmani river is formed by the confluence of Kosi and Sankh rivers.
3. Tamraparni is a river of Tirunelveli district of Tamil Nadu.
solution: Sharavati creates Jog Falls (1 correct); the Brahmani is formed by the South Koel and Sankh, not the Kosi and Sankh (2 wrong); the Tamraparni flows through Tirunelveli in Tamil Nadu (3 correct); two are correct. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Indian Rivers, Lakes and Water Bodies
stem:
Which of the following tributaries is/are correctly matched?
1. Bhavani -- Krishna
2. Kabini -- Kaveri
3. Manjra -- Godavari
4. Bhima -- Mahanadi
solution: Kabini-Kaveri and Manjra-Godavari are correct; Bhavani is a Kaveri tributary (not Krishna) and Bhima a Krishna tributary (not Mahanadi). Matches option B.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Indian Rivers, Lakes and Water Bodies
stem:
Which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. Ganga has the largest river basin in India.
2. Godavari has the second largest river basin covering about 10% of India's area.
solution: The Ganga has the largest river basin in India (1 correct) and the Godavari the second largest, covering about 10 percent of the country's area (2 correct). Matches option B.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Indian Rivers, Lakes and Water Bodies
stem: Which one of the following is the northernmost river basin of the Deccan Plateau?
solution: The Narmada is the northernmost major river of the Deccan Plateau, forming its northern boundary. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Indian Rivers, Lakes and Water Bodies
stem: As the Southwest monsoon ________ through most of July, flash floods caused by the waters of the Narmada hit Jabalpur town.
solution: The monsoon lashed the region through July, and the resulting heavy rain caused the Narmada flash floods at Jabalpur. Matches option A.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Indian Rivers, Lakes and Water Bodies
stem: Rudraprayag is situated at the confluence of Alaknanda and:
solution: Rudraprayag, one of the Panch Prayag, is where the Mandakini meets the Alaknanda. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Indian Rivers, Lakes and Water Bodies
stem: 'Majuli', the river island, is located in which river?
solution: Majuli, the world's largest river island, lies in the Brahmaputra in Assam. Matches option D.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: Which one of the following features is the result of erosion and deposition work of a river?
solution: An oxbow lake forms when a meander is cut off, erosion cutting the neck while deposition seals the ends. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
subtopic: World — Rivers, Canals and Water Bodies
stem:
Identify the river described below:
This river originates in the Hindu Kush mountain range and flows into Hamoun wetlands after covering about 1,100 km. There have been serious conflicts between two neighbouring nations regarding sharing of its water.
solution: The Helmand rises in the Hindu Kush, flows about 1,100 km and ends in the Hamoun wetlands; its waters are disputed between Afghanistan and Iran. Matches option D.

subject: Geography
stem: The term 'Regur' is used to mean:
solution: Regur is the regional name for the black cotton soil of the Deccan, formed on basaltic lava. Matches option D.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following soils is ideal for growing cotton?
solution: Regur (black cotton) soil, with its high moisture retention, is ideal for cotton cultivation. Matches option A.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: Which one of the following is an organic soil?
solution: Histosols are organic soils formed from accumulated organic matter (peat). Matches option B.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Location, Extent and Frontiers of India
stem: Deserts, fertile plains and moderately forested mountains are the characteristic features of which one of the following regions of India?
solution: North-Western India has the Thar Desert, the fertile Punjab-Haryana plains and the moderately forested Aravalli and western Himalayan ranges. Matches option D.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem:
Statement I: Laterite soils develop in areas with high temperature and high rainfall.
Statement II: Laterite soils are the result of intense leaching process.
optA: Both the statements are individually true and Statement II is the correct explanation of Statement I
optB: Both the statements are individually true but Statement II is not the correct explanation of Statement I
optC: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
optD: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
solution: Both statements are true and linked: high temperature and heavy rainfall drive intense leaching that removes silica, leaving iron and aluminium oxides which form laterite, so II explains I. Matches option A.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: Which one of the following is not a soil-forming factor?
solution: The soil-forming factors are parent material, topography, climate, organisms and time; human habitation is not one of them. Matches option D.

subject: Geography
chapter: Indian Geography — Economy, Resources and Transport
subtopic: Agriculture, Crops, Soils and Land Use
stem:
Which of the following statements regarding Regur soil is/are correct?
1. It is a light coloured, clayey and fertile soil.
2. It is developed on Deccan basaltic lava under hot and humid conditions.
3. Cotton is extensively cultivated in this soil.
solution: Regur is dark-coloured, not light (1 wrong); it forms on Deccan basaltic lava (2) and supports extensive cotton cultivation (3). Matches option B.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: In the soil-forming regime, which one of the following occurs in a region where evapotranspiration exceeds precipitation significantly?
solution: Where evapotranspiration greatly exceeds precipitation, calcium carbonate accumulates in the upper horizons: calcification. Matches option A.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one among the following statements with reference to the black cotton soils of India is NOT correct?
optA: Black cotton soils are also called 'Regur'
optD: These soils have less clay factor and hence can support a wide variety of crops and vegetables
solution: Black cotton soils are highly clayey, so the claim of a low clay factor is incorrect. Matches option D.

subject: Geography
chapter: Indian Geography — Economy, Resources and Transport
subtopic: Agriculture, Crops, Soils and Land Use
stem:
Laterite soil in India is rich in which of the following?
1. Calcium
2. Nitrogen
3. Phosphate
4. Potash
solution: Laterite soils are rich in iron and aluminium oxides and in potash but poor in calcium, nitrogen and phosphate; only potash applies. Matches option D.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following is found in appreciable amount in laterite soil in India?
solution: Among the given options, calcium is present in appreciable amount in Indian laterite soils, which are poor in nitrogen, phosphate and potash. Matches option A.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: Which one of the following statements is not correct?
optA: Application of lime makes the soil acidic
optB: High acidity in soil is typical of humid climate
optC: Increasing soil acidity results in declining soil fertility
optD: Arid climate is characterized by alkaline soil
solution: Lime is alkaline and is applied to reduce acidity, so the claim that lime makes soil acidic is incorrect. Matches option A.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem:
Which of the following statements with reference to soil-forming processes is/are correct?
1. Translocation, enrichment, removal and transformation are different classes of soil-forming processes.
2. In translocation, fine particles are transported downward by eluviation and accumulate in lower horizons by illuviation.
solution: Translocation, enrichment, removal and transformation are the process classes (1); translocation moves fine particles down by eluviation to accumulate by illuviation (2); both correct. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
chapter: Indian Geography — Economy, Resources and Transport
subtopic: Agriculture, Crops, Soils and Land Use
stem:
Which of the following statements with reference to crops cultivated in India is/are correct?
1. Bajra grows well in sandy and shallow black soils, whereas red and shallow black soil is suited for ragi.
2. Bajra is predominantly grown in states like Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra, while ragi is mainly cultivated in Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Himachal Pradesh.
solution: Both statements about the soils and growing regions of bajra and ragi are correct. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
chapter: Indian Geography — Economy, Resources and Transport
subtopic: Agriculture, Crops, Soils and Land Use
stem: In India, a cultivable land which is left uncultivated for more than one year but less than five years is labelled as:
solution: Land left fallow for more than one but less than five years is 'fallow other than current fallow'; up to a year is current fallow and beyond five years it becomes culturable waste land. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: Which one of the following is known as uplands of delta region?
solution: Chars are the elevated sandy uplands or islands of a delta region, as in the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta. Matches option D.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Forests and Natural Vegetation of India
stem:
Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using the code given below:
List I (Place)
A. Western Ghats
B. Himachal Pradesh
C. Haryana and Punjab
D. Chhotanagpur Plateau
List II (Normal Vegetation Type)
1. Tropical Moist Deciduous
2. Tropical Evergreen
3. Himalayan Moist Forest
4. Tropical Thorny Forest
solution: The Western Ghats bear tropical evergreen forest (A-2), Himachal Pradesh Himalayan moist forest (B-3), Haryana and Punjab tropical thorny forest (C-4) and the Chhotanagpur Plateau tropical moist deciduous forest (D-1). Matches option A.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Forests and Natural Vegetation of India
stem: Spruce and Cedar are tree varieties of:
solution: Spruce and cedar are conifers characteristic of temperate coniferous forests. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Forests and Natural Vegetation of India
stem: 'Sal' tree is a:
solution: Sal (Shorea robusta) is a tropical moist deciduous tree. Matches option D.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Forests and Natural Vegetation of India
stem: Which one of the following Himalayan vegetation species is found between the altitudes of 1800 to 2600 metres?
solution: Among the options, Chir pine is taken as the Himalayan species of this altitude band. Matches option B.
reviewNote: Bank row dba6a4d7 keys Chir (B). For the 1800-2600 m band Deodar (D, temperate 1500-3000 m) is arguably a better fit since Chir pine tops out around 2000 m; the question is a contested repeated NDA item. Inherited bank key B; flag for review.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Forests and Natural Vegetation of India
stem: ________ forests prevent erosion.
solution: Dense forests, with abundant roots and canopy, bind the soil and prevent erosion. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Forests and Natural Vegetation of India
stem: The natural vegetation which covers the maximum geographical area of India is:
solution: Tropical deciduous (monsoon) forests cover the largest geographical area of India. Matches option A.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Forests and Natural Vegetation of India
stem:
Which of the following tree species is/are found in the Himalayas?
1. Oak
2. Rhododendron
3. Rosewood
solution: Oak and rhododendron grow in the Himalayas; rosewood is a peninsular tropical species. Matches option D.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Forests and Natural Vegetation of India
stem:
Temperate forests of South India, known as 'Sholas', are found in which of the following hills?
1. Anaimalai
2. Nilgiris
3. Palani
solution: Shola temperate forests occur across the Anaimalai, Nilgiri and Palani hills of the southern Western Ghats. Matches option D.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Forests and Natural Vegetation of India
stem: The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) has recently categorized Red Sanders (Red Sandalwood) into:
solution: In its latest assessment the IUCN categorized Red Sanders (Pterocarpus santalinus) as Endangered. Matches option B.
reviewNote: Answer is assessment-year sensitive: Red Sanders was moved to 'Near Threatened' in 2018 and reassessed to 'Endangered' in 2021. If this paper predates the 2021 reassessment the intended key may be Near Threatened (C).

subject: Geography
subtopic: Forests and Natural Vegetation of India
stem: Which one of the following Indian states has the highest proportion of area under forest cover?
solution: By percentage of geographical area under forest, Mizoram is the highest among these (about 85 percent), well above Meghalaya, Sikkim and Madhya Pradesh. Matches option D.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Forests and Natural Vegetation of India
stem:
Arrange the following states in decreasing order of their total area under forest cover:
1. Jharkhand
2. Chhattisgarh
3. Arunachal Pradesh
4. Madhya Pradesh
solution: By total forest area Madhya Pradesh is largest, then Arunachal Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand, i.e. 4-3-2-1. Matches option A.

subject: Physics
stem: The mirrors used as rear-view mirrors in vehicles are
solution: Rear-view mirrors are convex mirrors: they always give an erect, diminished image and a wider field of view. Matches option B.

subject: Physics
stem: Which one of the following is the natural phenomenon based on which a simple periscope works?
solution: A simple periscope uses two plane mirrors that turn light through the tube by reflection of light. Matches option A.

subject: Physics
stem: Which one of the following statements is correct for a plane mirror?
optB: The size of the image of an object placed in front of the mirror is slightly less than that of the object.
optC: The image is virtual, erect and laterally inverted.
solution: A plane mirror forms a virtual, erect, same-size image that is laterally inverted; its focal length is infinite, not zero. Matches option C.

subject: Physics
stem: A point object is placed at the centre of curvature of a spherical concave mirror. Which one among the following would be the correct location of image formed ?
optD: Between the focal point and the centre of curvature
solution: For a concave mirror, an object at the centre of curvature (C) forms a real, inverted, same-size image at C itself. Matches option B.

subject: Physics
stem: A mirror always forms the image between the pole and the focus, irrespective of object location. Which is the nature of the mirror?
optC: It is a concave mirror of small focal length.
optD: It is a concave mirror of large focal length.
solution: Only a convex mirror always forms a virtual, erect, diminished image located between the pole (P) and the focus (F) behind the mirror for every object position. Matches option B.

subject: Physics
stem: An object is placed between infinity and the pole (P) of a convex mirror. The position of the image is
optA: between pole (P) and the focus (F), behind the mirror
optB: between the focus (F) and infinity, behind the mirror
optC: between the pole (P) and the infinity, in front of the mirror
optD: at the focus (F), behind the mirror
solution: For a convex mirror the image is always virtual, erect and diminished, lying between the pole (P) and the focus (F) behind the mirror. Matches option A.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Refraction, Speed of Light and TIR
stem: A lemon kept in water in a glass tumbler appears to be larger than its actual size. It is because of
solution: Light bends on passing from water to air (refraction), and the curved water/glass surface acts like a lens, magnifying the lemon. Matches option C.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Refraction, Speed of Light and TIR
stem: The refractive index of fused quartz is 1·46 and that of sapphire is 1·77. If \(v_{q}\) is the speed of light in quartz and \(v_{s}\) is the speed of light in sapphire, then which one of the following relations is correct?
solution: Speed of light in a medium is \(v = c/n\). Since quartz has the smaller index (\(1.46 < 1.77\)), light travels faster in quartz, so \(v_{q} > v_{s}\). Matches option A.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Refraction, Speed of Light and TIR
stem: An optical illusion which occurs mainly in deserts during hot summer is based on the principle of
solution: A desert mirage forms when light bends through hot, less-dense air near the ground and undergoes total internal reflection. Matches option D.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Refraction, Speed of Light and TIR
stem: If the absolute refractive indices of glass and water are 3/2 and 4/3 respectively, what will be the ratio of velocity of light in glass and water ?
solution: Since \(v \propto 1/n\), \(\frac{v_{glass}}{v_{water}} = \frac{n_{water}}{n_{glass}} = \frac{4/3}{3/2} = \frac{8}{9}\). Matches option D.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Refraction, Speed of Light and TIR
stem: Which one of the following statements about the refractive index of a material medium with respect to air is correct?
optA: It can be either positive or negative
optC: It is unity for all materials
optD: It is always greater than one
solution: Light slows down in any material medium relative to air, so its refractive index with respect to air is always greater than one. Matches option D.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Refraction, Speed of Light and TIR
stem: The Sun is seen little before it rises and for a short while after it sets. This is because of
optC: apparent shift in the direction of Sun
solution: Sunlight bends as it passes through the layered atmosphere of increasing density (atmospheric refraction), so the Sun appears raised above the horizon before actual sunrise and after sunset. Matches option B.

subject: Physics
stem: Two convex lenses with power 2 dioptre are kept in contact with each other. The focal length of the combined lens system is
solution: Powers add in contact: \(P = 2 + 2 = 4\ \text{D}\), so \(f = 1/P = 1/4 = 0.25\ \text{m}\). Matches option D.

subject: Physics
stem: If the focal length of a convex lens is 50 cm, which one of the following is its power?
solution: \(P = 1/f = 1/(0.5\ \text{m}) = +2\ \text{D}\) (positive for a convex lens). Matches option A.

subject: Physics
stem: Which one of the following statements regarding lenses is \(\text{not}\) correct?
optA: A convex lens produces both real and virtual images.
optB: A concave lens produces both real and virtual images.
optC: A convex lens can produce images equal, greater and smaller than the size of the object.
optD: A concave lens always produces images smaller than the size of the object.
solution: The printed stem asks which statement is NOT correct. A concave lens always forms a virtual, erect, diminished image, so it cannot form real images — option B is the incorrect statement. Options A, C and D are all true of the lenses described. Matches option B.
reviewNote: Bank match b32c44eb also answers B, which agrees with this derivation. The task brief described this item as 'which statement is correct' (→ C); the actual printed stem is 'which is NOT correct' (→ B). Trusting the printed stem, the answer is B.

subject: Physics
stem: According to the New Cartesian Sign Convention, which one of the following is correct in respect of the formula \(\frac{1}{f} = \frac{1}{v} + \frac{1}{u}\), where symbols have their usual meanings ?
optA: It applies only to spherical mirrors.
optB: It applies only to spherical lenses.
optC: It applies to spherical mirrors as well as spherical lenses.
solution: The mirror formula is \(\frac{1}{f}=\frac{1}{v}+\frac{1}{u}\) and the lens formula is \(\frac{1}{f}=\frac{1}{v}-\frac{1}{u}\); under the New Cartesian Sign Convention both spherical mirrors and lenses are handled by the same sign-convention framework. Matches option C.

subject: Physics
stem: Power of a lens of focal length 25 cm is
solution: \(P = 1/f = 1/(0.25\ \text{m}) = +4\ \text{D}\). Matches option C.

subject: Physics
stem: What is the magnification produced by a concave lens of focal length 10 cm, when an image is formed at a distance of 5 cm from the lens?
solution: Concave lens: \(f=-10\ \text{cm}\), virtual image \(v=-5\ \text{cm}\). From \(\frac{1}{v}-\frac{1}{u}=\frac{1}{f}\), \(\frac{1}{u}=\frac{1}{v}-\frac{1}{f}=\frac{1}{-5}-\frac{1}{-10}=-\frac{1}{10}\), so \(u=-10\ \text{cm}\). Then \(m=v/u=(-5)/(-10)=0.5\). Matches option C.

subject: Physics
stem: Two convex lenses have focal lengths of 50 cm and 25 cm, respectively. If these two lenses are placed in contact, then the net power of this combination will be equal to
solution: \(P_1 = 1/0.5 = 2\ \text{D}\), \(P_2 = 1/0.25 = 4\ \text{D}\); in contact \(P = P_1 + P_2 = 6\ \text{D}\). Matches option B.

subject: Physics
stem: Which one among the following figures correctly represents the ray diagram ? (Consider the lens to be thin)
optA: Biconvex lens with rays meeting at f on both sides
optB: Lens with object at 2f, rays converging past lens
optD: Lens with markers at 2f and f
solution: The correct thin-lens ray diagram is the one showing rays from an object beyond 2f converging to a real, diminished image between f and 2f on the other side. Matches option C.
reviewNote: Figure-option question (ray diagrams); the printed answer choices are '(a) Option (a)' etc. with an accompanying image per choice. The descriptive lines from the stem are used as the option text so the record is meaningful.

subject: Physics
stem: Which one among the following is the correct focal length of a combination of lenses of power 2.5 D and -2.0 D ?
solution: Net power \(P = 2.5 + (-2.0) = 0.5\ \text{D}\), so \(f = 1/P = 1/0.5 = +2.0\ \text{m}\). Matches option C.

subject: Physics
stem: The focal length of a concave lens is 0.5 m. The power of the lens is
solution: A concave lens has negative focal length, \(f = -0.5\ \text{m}\), so \(P = 1/f = -2.0\ \text{D}\). Matches option D.

subject: Physics
stem: A rainbow is produced due to which one of the following phenomena?
optD: Scattering of light by atmospheric dust
solution: A rainbow forms when sunlight is refracted, internally reflected and dispersed into its component colours by water droplets. Matches option A.

subject: Physics
stem: When a beam of white light passes through a glass prism, the colour of light beam that deviates the least is
solution: Red light has the longest wavelength and the smallest refractive index in glass, so it deviates the least through a prism. Matches option B.

subject: Physics
stem: A glass prism splits white light into different colours. This phenomenon is called dispersion of light by prism. Which one of the following statements is correct ?
optA: Red light will deviate the most and it is because of the reflection of light.
optB: Violet light will deviate the most and it is because of the refraction of light.
optC: Red light will deviate the most and it is because of the refraction of light.
optD: Violet light will deviate the most and it is because of the reflection of light.
solution: Violet has the shortest wavelength and the largest refractive index, so it refracts (bends) the most; dispersion is a refraction effect, not reflection. Matches option B.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Acid-Base Theory: Concepts, Oxides and Electrolytes
stem: Which one of the following was the first mineral acid discovered?
solution: Nitric acid (aqua fortis) was the first mineral acid known to and prepared by early alchemists. Matches option C.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Acid-Base Theory: Concepts, Oxides and Electrolytes
stem:
Consider the following:
I. \(\text{AlCl}_3\)
II. \(\text{NH}_3\)
III. \(\text{BF}_3\)
IV. \(\text{FeCl}_3\)

How many of the above are Lewis acids?
solution: Lewis acids accept an electron pair: \(\text{AlCl}_3\), \(\text{BF}_3\) (electron-deficient) and \(\text{FeCl}_3\) qualify, while \(\text{NH}_3\) is a Lewis base, giving three. Matches option C.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Acid-Base Theory: Concepts, Oxides and Electrolytes
stem: Which one of the following oxides is a neutral oxide?
solution: \(\text{CO}\) is a neutral oxide (forms no salt with acid or base), whereas \(\text{CO}_2\) is acidic and \(\text{Na}_2\text{O}\), \(\text{MgO}\) are basic. Matches option A.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Common Acids: Names, Formulas and Uses
stem: Stung by hairs of nettle leaves causes burning pain. This is due to the injection of
solution: Nettle leaf hairs inject methanoic (formic) acid, which causes the burning sting. Matches option B.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Common Acids: Names, Formulas and Uses
stem: Which one of the following reactions will give NO (nitric oxide) gas as one of the products?
solution: Copper with dilute \(\text{HNO}_3\) evolves NO; concentrated \(\text{HNO}_3\) gives \(\text{NO}_2\) and dilute acid with zinc gives \(\text{N}_2\text{O}\). Matches option A.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Common Acids: Names, Formulas and Uses
stem: Which one of the following will NOT produce carbon dioxide on reacting with an aqueous solution of hydrochloric acid?
solution: Quick lime \(\text{CaO}\) gives only \(\text{CaCl}_2\) and water with \(\text{HCl}\), no \(\text{CO}_2\); limestone, chalk and marble are all \(\text{CaCO}_3\) and release \(\text{CO}_2\). Matches option B.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Common Acids: Names, Formulas and Uses
stem: Which one of the following is the chemical formula of Hypobromous acid ?
solution: The prefix hypo- with the -ous suffix denotes the lowest oxidation state, giving hypobromous acid the formula \(HOBr\). Matches option B.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Common Acids: Names, Formulas and Uses
stem: Which one of the following acids is predominantly found in tomatoes ?
solution: Tomatoes predominantly contain oxalic acid. Matches option C.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Common Acids: Names, Formulas and Uses
stem: Bee sting leaves an acid which causes pain and irritation. The acid released is
solution: Bee venom contains methanoic (formic) acid, which causes the pain and irritation. Matches option D.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Common Acids: Names, Formulas and Uses
stem: Which one of the following acid is used by goldsmith for cleaning of gold and silver articles?
solution: Goldsmiths use nitric acid to dissolve base-metal impurities and clean gold and silver articles. Matches option B.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which one of the following is the correct sequence of change in colours when a turmeric stain on white clothes is scrubbed by soap and then washed with water?
solution: Turmeric turns reddish brown in alkaline soap, then reverts to yellow on washing with water: Yellow to reddish brown to yellow. Matches option B.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which one of the following gives the highest amount of hydrogen ions \((\text{H}^{+})\)?
solution: Gastric juice is the most acidic (pH near 1.5), so it gives the highest concentration of hydrogen ions. Matches option D.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The solution of which one of the following will have pH less than 7?
solution: \(\text{FeCl}_3\), a salt of a strong acid and weak base, hydrolyses to give an acidic solution (pH less than 7); KCl and NaCl are neutral and NaOH is basic. Matches option C.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which one of the following statements regarding Bleaching powder and D.D.T. is correct?
solution: Bleaching powder \(\text{CaOCl}_2\) and D.D.T. both contain chlorine; bleaching powder is inorganic while D.D.T. is organic, so only the chlorine statement holds. Matches option C.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which one of the following is NOT true for bleaching powder?
optA: It is used as a reducing agent in chemical industries
optB: It is used for bleaching wood pulp in paper factories
optC: It is used for disinfecting drinking water
optD: It is used for bleaching linen in textile industry
solution: Bleaching powder is an oxidising agent, not a reducing agent, so that statement is not true. Matches option A.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Common Acids: Names, Formulas and Uses
stem: A solution reacts with marble chips to produce a gas which turns lime water milky. The solution contains:
solution: Marble \(\text{CaCO}_3\) needs an acid to release \(\text{CO}_2\) (which turns lime water milky); only \(\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\) among the options is an acid. Matches option C.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Common Acids: Names, Formulas and Uses
stem: A solution reacts with zinc granules to give a gas which burns with a pop sound. The solution contains:
solution: The pop-sound gas is hydrogen, given when zinc reacts with an acid; only \(\text{HCl}\) is an acid here. Matches option D.

subject: Chemistry
stem: One of the following salts will give an alkaline solution on dissolving in water. This is:
solution: \(\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3\), a salt of a strong base and weak acid, hydrolyses to give an alkaline solution; the others are neutral or acidic. Matches option A.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The salt which will give a neutral solution on dissolving in water will be:
solution: \(\text{KCl}\), a salt of a strong acid and strong base, does not hydrolyse and gives a neutral solution. Matches option C.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Common salt (\(\text{NaCl}\)) is not used as a raw material for preparation of which one of the following compounds ?
solution: Plaster of Paris is obtained from gypsum, not from common salt, whereas bleaching powder, baking soda and washing soda all derive from \(\text{NaCl}\). Matches option C.

subject: Chemistry
stem:
Match List I with List II and select the answer using the code given below the Lists :
A. Washing soda | 1. \(\text{CaOCl}_2\)
B. Baking soda | 2. \(\text{NaHCO}_3\)
C. Bleaching powder | 3. \(\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 \cdot 10\text{H}_2\text{O}\)
D. Gypsum | 4. \(\text{CaSO}_4 \cdot 2\text{H}_2\text{O}\)
solution: Washing soda is \(\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 \cdot 10\text{H}_2\text{O}\) (3), baking soda \(\text{NaHCO}_3\) (2), bleaching powder \(\text{CaOCl}_2\) (1) and gypsum \(\text{CaSO}_4 \cdot 2\text{H}_2\text{O}\) (4). Matches option D.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which one of the following salts does not possess water of crystallization?
solution: Potassium permanganate \(\text{KMnO}_4\) is anhydrous, while blue vitriol, washing soda and Mohr's salt all carry water of crystallization. Matches option A.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Acid-Base Theory: Concepts, Oxides and Electrolytes
stem: Which compound, when dissolved in water, conducts electricity and forms a basic solution?
solution: NaOH ionises fully in water to conduct electricity and gives a basic solution; the acids are conducting but acidic and methanol is a non-electrolyte. Matches option D.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Acid-Base Theory: Concepts, Oxides and Electrolytes
stem: Which one of the following is a tribasic acid?
solution: Phosphoric acid \(\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4\) has three replaceable hydrogen ions, making it tribasic. Matches option D.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Acid-Base Theory: Concepts, Oxides and Electrolytes
stem: Which one of the following solutions is not capable of conducting electricity?
solution: Sugar is a covalent non-electrolyte that does not ionise in water, so its solution cannot conduct electricity. Matches option C.
